record.title: Prevalence of different types of arrhythmias in canine babesiosis and ehrlichiosis
record.journal: International Journal of Advanced Biochemistry Research
record.abstract: The study assessed cardiac arrhythmias in dogs naturally infected with tick-borne diseases in Palampur. Of 2,755 dogs examined, 465 (16.87%) were haemoparasite-positive and 108 (23.22%) exhibited electrocardiographic abnormalities. Babesia gibsoni was the predominant pathogen, followed by Ehrlichia canis. Major arrhythmias included sinus arrhythmia, tachycardia, low-voltage QRS complexes, QRS notching and ST-segment deviations. Middle-aged male dogs were most affected. The findings highlight significant cardiac involvement in tick-borne infections and underline the importance of routine ECG for early detection and management.

screening.species: B. gibsoni (suspected; mixed with E. canis)
screening.rationale: ECG abnormalities in dogs with tick-borne infections, mostly B. gibsoni; cardiac involvement, though mixed with ehrlichiosis.
